# Phobos Medical: equipment and item reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/update-item-reference.ps1. Edit config/item-reference.json, not this file. -->

Current source candidate: **0.3.0**. Game target: **1.0.1.5**. Values below come from offline definitions; they do not establish installation, gameplay validation or a live merchant quote.

Phobos Medical adds the Halewright Ward-3 Medical Bed, a powered sickbay bed that takes an unconscious casualty, lets the injured rest awake, and keeps its patient recuperating with the game's own medical-rest healing while it has power and air. The Halewright Vigil-2 Patient Monitor stands beside a Ward-3 and shows its patient's readings and alerts. See [the player guide](medical-player-guide.md).

**Reading prices:** credits per complete object at the stated condition, before shop margins, market effects, negotiation and extra wear. Pristine retail can cost more. Mass is the empty/dry definition or fresh commodity template; saved contents and variable recovery packets can weigh differently. Dismantle value is the sum of all listed outputs at base value, excluding labour and tools.

**Repair and Restore:** Repair fixes a damaged form and uses up its parts, as the game's own repairs do. Restore reduces wear on functional equipment in place; it does not grant pristine status. Empty cargo and follow the machine’s local maintenance guards first. Work speed depends on crew, tools and current condition.

**Finding stock:** the generated percentages are defaults per eligible native stock/loot roll, not per ship or guaranteed shop availability. Offers are additive, may be independent, and require normal restocking. Merchant offers request the listed finite lot when successful; separate world-loot branches retain their own listed quantities. Configuration, capacity and native generation rules still apply; loading an existing save does not refill its inventories.

**Stacking:** limits below apply to loose items on the ground or in compatible containers; 1 means no multi-item stack. Installed equipment remains individual. Limits count objects, not kilograms, and do not change merchant lot sizes or per-object contents.

## Ward-3 Medical Bed

A 3 x 5 powered medical bed. While installed, intact, powered and in a room with air, its patient recuperates: the game's own medical-rest healing (wound, blood and infection recovery and pain threshold), the same as the vanilla Infirmaway gives a sleeper. Without power or air it is an ordinary bed. A 3 x 2 drawer holds dressings, splints and medicines.

**Use:** Install through FURN with its head against a wall carrying power. Drag an unconscious person to it and choose Lay patient here; order an injured crew member to Rest and recover; or Sleep in it when tired. Switch on Send injured crew here and a free bed calls the worst-off injured crew member. The Control Panel shows the patient and a short health reading, and sets whether anyone may sleep in it or only the injured. 22.5 W idle, 150 W while caring.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below: new at the K-Leg furnishings kiosk, worn from the K-Leg fixer, broken at the K-Leg supply kiosk, refurbished at the Venus scrap kiosk, and at the regional supply kiosks. About one engineering-loot roll in fifty yields a Ward-3, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → FURN. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Its treatment cartridges and folded arms are 2075 styling; the healing is the game's own medical rest. Uninstalling or dismantling is refused while someone is in it. Under its care a weightless patient heals at the normal rate (the game otherwise slows it to a twentieth). It does not dress wounds yet.

Full operating instructions: [Ward-3 Medical Bed guide](medical-player-guide.md).

<a id="vigil2"></a>

## Vigil-2 Patient Monitor

A 2 x 2 bedside monitor cart. It watches the patient of the Ward-3 it touches and shows blood lost, infection, pain and every wound with the change over the last hour, and posts a caution when a figure rises to its alert level or a wound starts bleeding. It never treats or heals. It stores nothing.

**Use:** Install through APPS beside a Ward-3, touching it or one tile away, with its back against a wall carrying power. Open its Control Panel for the readings; set which touching bed it watches and whether it posts alerts. 10 W idle, 60 W while watching.

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below, on the Ward-3's routes. A rare engineering-loot find, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Its hour's trend is kept in memory and starts again after a reload. Readings it cannot take say so rather than showing zero.

Full operating instructions: [Vigil-2 Patient Monitor guide](medical-player-guide.md).

## Evidence and upkeep

Item names, dry/template masses, prices, service bills, salvage outputs, placement tabs, stock probabilities and table recipes are generated from current Phobos definitions. **Blue Bottle Games’ Ostranauts** native `DataCO.GetBasePrice` supplies the offline valuation used here ([developer’s game page](https://bluebottlegames.com/games/ostranauts)). That page identifies the game; the actual numeric evidence is the locally inspected assembly, whose hash is retained in the generated data snapshot. No proprietary source or game assembly is distributed.

Function/use explanations are maintained in the reviewed catalogue. All fictional prices, yields and simplified processing are Phobos gameplay choices. Research attribution remains beside the relevant claims in the linked operating/research guides.
